scope: Planning Board methodology bridge for direct-investment profits, industry aggregation, and rest-of-world treatment
authority: Puerto Rico Planning Board / Junta de Planificacion

source.title: Metodologia de Procesos de Cuentas Economicas / Metodologia Cuentas Sociales

findings.description: The methodology states that a CRIM-based direct-investment-firm study collects profit information used to prepare base data by industrial sector.
findings.implication: A sectoral statistical production mechanism exists in the documented methodology; this does not prove that a FY2025 public sector table is currently published.

findings.description: The base study is designed to cover the universe of direct-investment firms, maintain a register, trace missing returns, and prioritize important firms; sectors with few firms should be covered as a universe.
findings.implication: Text-search absence or a partial company list cannot establish the direct-investment firm denominator.

findings.description: The methodology calls for a Balance of Payments unit database combining all sources for direct-investment-firm profits over a series of years, drawing on CRIM/tax-return information, questionnaires, Income Net data, and Hacienda information.
findings.implication: Current published aggregates may derive from confidential/multi-source firm-level inputs; public industry context cannot substitute for the missing published allocation.

findings.description: When base-year figures exist, intermediate-year estimates may be established with indicators and later revised; calendar-year company profits should be converted to fiscal-year basis.
findings.implication: A current annual sector estimate may contain estimation/revision layers and cannot be reconstructed reliably from a single unrelated current-year proxy.

findings.description: Income Net survey information is collected by company and aggregated by industry following NAICS; JP publishes Income Net tables by industrial sector, legal sector, and payment type.
findings.implication: Income Net has a company-to-industry source architecture but remains a distinct measurement domain from direct-investment profits unless an authoritative bridge is supplied.

findings.description: IP-11 is used for Hacienda/tax-return-derived Income Net information and can support sales, wages, profits, interest paid, and interest received estimates.
findings.implication: IP-11 is a high-priority source instrument for methodology/source-lineage exhaustion, not itself a public FY2025 DI-profit sector table.

findings.description: Administrative and other charges assigned by parent companies to Puerto Rico direct-investment firms are treated as payments deducted in establishing profits and recorded as miscellaneous payments from a Puerto Rico resident to a nonresident.
findings.implication: Parent-company charges are a separate rest-of-world payment mechanism and must not be conflated with the direct-investment-profit aggregate.

hard_boundary: Documented methodology is evidence of how the statistical system can construct sector-level direct-investment-profit estimates; it is not evidence of the actual FY2025 sector amounts.
